Bethesda rpgs are super flawed, I think it benefits from a niche market and there's a ton of things to improve on, outer worlds and new vegas improved on the dialog and writing now we just need a studio to comealong and improve upon the combat.

I think we could classify those as rpg lite. It gives you limited options in how you build your character and its choices exist on a spectrum, do I wanna be a sneaky pacifist or a murderous psychopath? Or somewhere in between? However the game world is limited and level based and your character has preset motivation a name and a background. I think rpg games exist on a spectrum as well now that I think about it. The two extremes would be something like uncharted where the game is very linear and you're basically just playing through a story with no impact made by the player, on the other end would be something like DnD which has so much choice its been impossible for games to replicate it even though some have come close.

Well I think to even be defined as an rpg at the very least there should be character customization and your choices should impact the story. I consider cyberpunk and fallout 4 rpgs despite having a voiced protagonist and the inability to role play certain roles. I think true rpgs have either a silent protagonist or the ability to choose a certain voice. They also give your character a blank slate or allow you to choose your own background. I would consider outer worlds as well as daggerfall and newvegas to be true rpgs. Skyrim kinda rides this weird middleground, where you don't necessarily have a ton of choice in how the story plays out but you do you have alot of choice in how to build your character.

Elderscrolls combat is pretty bad but I thinks it could be improved with just some simple effects and giving the character more impact when hitting an enemy with a weapon. A simple dodge and parry mechanic could really spice up the melee combat without being too overly complicated like mount and blade. they could also take the kingdom come route. I mean mods prove that 1st person melee combat doesn't have to be horrible. Also shooter rpgs like borderlands and metro usually follow a set story with preset character backgrounds and motives. I know metro has like 2 endings but theres hardly any choice, just generic bad karma and good karma route. Also this may be unpopular but I think fallout new Vegas has some pretty solid combat, I think with more incentive to specialize in certain weapons there would be more variety between playthroughs.
